Below is the canonical, implementation-grade specification for Offline-First Registry Mirroring, written as something you can build without guessing intent. No architecture fluff, no hand-waving.

OFFLINE-FIRST REGISTRY MIRRORING
Deterministic, Auditable, Authority-Preserving

0. NON-NEGOTIABLE GOALS
The mirroring layer must satisfy all of the following simultaneously:

Operate fully with zero network access

Preserve cryptographic trust offline

Maintain immutable history

Support eventual consistency when reconnected

Resolve conflicts deterministically

Respect registry RBAC and signatures

Never silently overwrite or merge state

If any of these fail, mirroring is invalid.

1. MIRROR ROLE IN THE SYSTEM
The mirror is not a cache.
It is a local authority replica.

Everything downstream reads from the mirror:

CLI

Unity plugin

Unreal plugin

CI jobs

Diff preview UI

Migration engine

The network registry is consulted only during explicit sync operations.

2. CANONICAL LOCAL MIRROR LAYOUT
Location (fixed):

~/.osl/registry/
Structure (authoritative):

~/.osl/registry/
├── index.yaml
├── packs/
│   └── osl.core/
│       ├── 1.0.0/
│       │   ├── pack.yaml
│       │   ├── templates/
│       │   ├── migrations/
│       │   └── signature/
│       ├── 1.1.0/
│       └── 1.2.0/
├── keys/
│   ├── trusted/
│   │   └── opensourceludus.pem
│   └── revoked/
├── audit/
│   └── mirror.log.jsonl
├── sync/
│   ├── last_sync.json
│   └── sync.log.jsonl
└── integrity/
    └── mirror.hash
Nothing outside this directory is required for correct operation.

3. MIRROR INDEX (index.yaml)
This is the single entry point for all lookups.

registry:
  schema_version: 1
  mirror_created: 2025-12-25T00:00:00Z
  last_verified: 2025-12-25T07:42:11Z

packs:
  osl.core:
    latest: 1.2.0
    versions:
      - 1.0.0
      - 1.1.0
      - 1.2.0
Rules:

Index is rewritten atomically

Index never references files that failed verification

Index is invalid if any referenced pack is missing or corrupt

4. TRUST MODEL (OFFLINE-SAFE)
4.1 Keys
Trusted public keys live in keys/trusted/

Revoked keys live in keys/revoked/

Keys are never fetched implicitly

4.2 Verification Rules
Every pack in the mirror must satisfy:

Hash integrity matches pack.yaml

Signature verifies against trusted key

Key is not revoked

Version is immutable and monotonic

Migration chain is complete

Failure of any rule invalidates the pack locally, regardless of upstream state.

5. STARTUP RESOLUTION FLOW (NO NETWORK)
On every CLI / plugin startup:

Load index.yaml

Verify index hash

Verify every referenced pack signature

Validate migration continuity

Enforce RBAC defaults

Proceed without touching the network

If verification fails:

System enters read-only preview mode

Apply, migrate, publish are blocked

Preview and diff remain available

No network retries. No warnings spam. Deterministic behavior.

6. SYNC OPERATION (EXPLICIT ONLY)
Command:

osl registry sync
6.1 Sync Steps
Fetch upstream index

Compare pack IDs and versions

Identify missing versions

Download missing packs only

Verify each pack (full signature + hash)

Write packs to temp directory

Update index.yaml atomically

Record audit + sync logs

6.2 Failure Handling
Partial sync allowed

Failed packs are discarded

Previous mirror remains authoritative

Sync never corrupts existing state

No destructive syncs. Ever.

7. CONFLICT RULES (DETERMINISTIC)
Scenario	Resolution
Same pack ID + same version + different hash	Reject
Same version, different signature	Reject
Local pack newer than upstream	Keep local
Revoked key upstream	Invalidate pack
Missing migration step	Block usage
Divergent lineage	Hard failure
There is no merge logic. Packs are immutable.

8. AUDIT CORRELATION (MANDATORY)
Every sync emits correlated audit records using the expanded schema.

Example:

{
  "event": "registry_sync_completed",
  "session_id": "uuid",

  "rejected_packs": [],

}
Mirror audit logs are append-only and immutable.

9. PLUGIN BEHAVIOR (READ-ONLY MIRROR)
Unity and Unreal plugins:

Read only from local mirror

Never fetch packs directly

Never bypass mirror verification

Display registry status clearly:

Registry: Offline (Mirrored)
Verified: Yes

CI never depends on live registry availability.

void UNH_GuardAuthorityComponent::HandleSeenPawn(APawn* Pawn)
{
    if (!Pawn || !Pawn->GetClass()->ImplementsInterface(UNH_InmateInterface::StaticClass()))
        return;

    if (INH_InmateInterface::Execute_IsViolationActive(Pawn))
    {
        OnViolationDetected.Broadcast(Pawn, EViolationType::OutOfBounds);
    }
}

private:
    TMap<FString, int32> ViolationCounts;
};
CPP
void UNH_PrisonAuthoritySubsystem::RegisterViolation(AActor* Violator, EViolationType Violation)
{
    if (!Violator) return;

    FString Id = INH_InmateInterface::Execute_GetInmateId(Violator);
    int32& Count = ViolationCounts.FindOrAdd(Id);
    Count++;

    if (Count >= 3)
    {
        TriggerLockdown();
    }
}
2.2 Lockdown Enforcement
void UNH_PrisonAuthoritySubsystem::TriggerLockdown()
{
    if (bIsLockdownActive) return;
    bIsLockdownActive = true;

    // Broadcast globally (BlueprintAssignable if you want)
}

void UNH_PrisonAuthoritySubsystem::EndLockdown()
{
    bIsLockdownActive = false;
}

1.2 Guard Patrol Component
NH_GuardPatrolComponent.h/.cpp
Header
UENUM(BlueprintType)
enum class EGuardState : uint8
{
    Patrol,
    Investigate,
    Alert,
    Lockdown
};

UCLASS(ClassGroup=(NH), meta=(BlueprintSpawnableComponent))
class UNH_GuardPatrolComponent : public UActorComponent
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    void StartPatrol(ANH_PatrolRoute* Route);

    void TickPatrol(float DeltaTime);

    void SetState(EGuardState NewState);

private:
    int32 CurrentIndex = 0;
    ANH_PatrolRoute* ActiveRoute = nullptr;
    EGuardState GuardState = EGuardState::Patrol;
};
CPP
void UNH_GuardPatrolComponent::StartPatrol(ANH_PatrolRoute* Route)
{
    ActiveRoute = Route;
    CurrentIndex = 0;
}

void UNH_GuardPatrolComponent::TickPatrol(float)
{
    if (!ActiveRoute || GuardState != EGuardState::Patrol) return;

    AActor* Target = ActiveRoute->GetWaypoint(CurrentIndex);
    if (!Target) return;

    // MoveTo handled by AIController

    if (FVector::Dist(GetOwner()->GetActorLocation(), Target->GetActorLocation()) < 100.f)
    {
        CurrentIndex = (CurrentIndex + 1) % ActiveRoute->Waypoints.Num();
    }
}
No behavior trees required. Those come later if you want to suffer.

def unity_task_templates() -> List[TaskTemplate]:
    return [
        TaskTemplate(
            name="player-movement",
            engine="unity",
            summary="3D character movement with camera-relative controls and jump.",
            checklist=[
                "Create a CharacterController-based movement script.",
                "Expose speed, jump height, and gravity in the inspector.",
                "Align movement to camera forward/right vectors.",
                "Use ground checks to reset vertical velocity.",
            ],
            copilot_prompt=UNITY_PROMPT
            + "\n\nTask: Implement a third-person player movement script.",
            code_skeleton=dedent(
                """
                using UnityEngine;

                [RequireComponent(typeof(CharacterController))]
                public class PlayerMovement : MonoBehaviour
                {
                    [Header("Movement")]
                    [SerializeField] private float moveSpeed = 5f;
                    [SerializeField] private float jumpHeight = 1.5f;
                    [SerializeField] private float gravity = -9.81f;
                    [SerializeField] private Transform cameraTransform;

                    private CharacterController controller;
                    private Vector3 velocity;

                    private void Awake()
                    {
                        controller = GetComponent<CharacterController>();
                    }

                    private void Update()
                    {
                        if (cameraTransform == null)
                        {
                            Debug.LogWarning("PlayerMovement: Missing cameraTransform reference.");
                            return;
                        }

                        bool isGrounded = controller.isGrounded;
                        if (isGrounded && velocity.y < 0f)
                        {
                            velocity.y = -2f; // keep grounded
                        }

                        float horizontal = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal");
                        float vertical = Input.GetAxis("Vertical");

                        Vector3 cameraForward = cameraTransform.forward;
                        cameraForward.y = 0f;
                        cameraForward.Normalize();
                        Vector3 cameraRight = cameraTransform.right;
                        cameraRight.y = 0f;
                        cameraRight.Normalize();

                        Vector3 move = (cameraForward * vertical + cameraRight * horizontal).normalized;
                        controller.Move(move * moveSpeed * Time.deltaTime);

                        if (Input.GetButtonDown("Jump") && isGrounded)
                        {
                            velocity.y = Mathf.Sqrt(jumpHeight * -2f * gravity);
                        }

                        velocity.y += gravity * Time.deltaTime;
                        controller.Move(velocity * Time.deltaTime);
                    }
                }
                """
            ).strip(),
        ),
        TaskTemplate(
            name="interaction-raycast",
            engine="unity",
            summary="Camera-based raycast interaction with UI prompt.",
            checklist=[
                "Cast a ray from the camera each frame.",
                "Detect objects with an IInteractable interface.",
                "Expose interact range and prompt UI text.",
                "Trigger interaction on input.",
            ],
            copilot_prompt=UNITY_PROMPT
            + "\n\nTask: Implement a raycast interaction system.",
            code_skeleton=dedent(
                """
                using UnityEngine;
                using UnityEngine.UI;

                public interface IInteractable
                {
                    string Prompt { get; }
                    void Interact();
                }

                public class InteractionRaycast : MonoBehaviour
                {
                    [SerializeField] private Camera playerCamera;
                    [SerializeField] private float interactRange = 3f;
                    [SerializeField] private Text promptText;

                    private IInteractable currentTarget;

                    private void Update()
                    {
                        if (playerCamera == null || promptText == null)
                        {
                            return;
                        }

                        currentTarget = null;
                        promptText.enabled = false;

                        Ray ray = new Ray(playerCamera.transform.position, playerCamera.transform.forward);
                        if (Physics.Raycast(ray, out RaycastHit hit, interactRange))
                        {
                            if (hit.collider.TryGetComponent(out IInteractable interactable))
                            {
                                currentTarget = interactable;
                                promptText.text = interactable.Prompt;
                                promptText.enabled = true;
                            }
                        }

                        if (currentTarget != null && Input.GetButtonDown("Fire1"))
                        {
                            currentTarget.Interact();
                        }
                    }
                }
                """
            ).strip(),

def filter_templates(engine: str | None, name: str | None) -> List[TaskTemplate]:
    templates = all_templates()
    if engine:
        templates = [template for template in templates if template.engine == engine]

    return templates

def parse_simple_yaml(raw: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    data_stack: list[Dict[str, Any] | list[Any]] = [{}]
    indent_stack = [0]

    for line in raw.splitlines():
        if not line.strip() or line.strip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        key_value = line.strip()

        while indent < indent_stack[-1]:
            data_stack.pop()
            indent_stack.pop()

        if key_value.startswith("- "):
            value = key_value[2:].strip()
            if not isinstance(data_stack[-1], list):
                raise MirrorError("Invalid YAML list structure.")
            data_stack[-1].append(coerce_scalar(value))
            continue

        if ":" in key_value:
            key, value = key_value.split(":", 1)
            key = key.strip()
            value = value.strip()
            if value == "":
                container: Dict[str, Any] | list[Any]
                if lookahead_is_list(raw, line):
                    container = []
                else:
                    container = {}
                data_stack[-1][key] = container
                data_stack.append(container)
                indent_stack.append(indent + 2)
            else:
                data_stack[-1][key] = coerce_scalar(value)
            continue

    if not isinstance(data_stack[0], dict):
        raise MirrorError("Invalid YAML document.")
    return data_stack[0]


def lookahead_is_list(raw: str, current_line: str) -> bool:
    lines = raw.splitlines()
    try:
        index = lines.index(current_line)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    for next_line in lines[index + 1 :]:
        if not next_line.strip() or next_line.strip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        return next_line.lstrip().startswith("-")
    return False


def coerce_scalar(value: str) -> Any:
    if value.lower() in {"true", "false"}:
        return value.lower() == "true"
    if value.isdigit():
        return int(value)
    return value


def dump_simple_yaml(data: Dict[str, Any], indent: int = 0) -> str:
    lines: list[str] = []
    pad = " " * indent
    for key, value in data.items():
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            lines.append(f"{pad}{key}:")
            lines.append(dump_simple_yaml(value, indent + 2))
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            lines.append(f"{pad}{key}:")
            for item in value:
                lines.append(f"{pad}  - {item}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{pad}{key}: {value}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def load_yaml(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if yaml:
        loaded = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
        if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
            raise MirrorError(f"YAML document at {path} is not a mapping.")
        return loaded
    return parse_simple_yaml(raw)


def dump_yaml(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if yaml:
        return yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False)
    return dump_simple_yaml(data)


def ensure_layout(root: Path) -> None:
    (root / "packs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / "keys" / "trusted").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / "keys" / "revoked").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / "audit").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / "sync").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / "integrity").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def index_path(root: Path) -> Path:
    return root / INDEX_FILENAME


def integrity_path(root: Path) -> Path:
    return root / INTEGRITY_FILENAME


def compute_sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(8192), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def write_integrity_hash(root: Path) -> None:
    index_file = index_path(root)
    if not index_file.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Cannot write integrity hash without index.yaml.")
    integrity = integrity_path(root)
    integrity.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    integrity.write_text(compute_sha256(index_file), encoding="utf-8")


def verify_integrity_hash(root: Path) -> None:
    integrity = integrity_path(root)
    index_file = index_path(root)
    if not integrity.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing integrity hash file.")
    if not index_file.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing index.yaml.")
    expected = integrity.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    actual = compute_sha256(index_file)
    if expected != actual:
        raise MirrorError("Index integrity hash mismatch.")


def build_index() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "registry": {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "mirror_created": utc_now(),
            "last_verified": utc_now(),
        },
        "packs": {},
    }


def write_index_atomic(root: Path, index_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    serialized = dump_yaml(index_data)
    tmp_dir = root / "integrity"
    tmp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", delete=False, dir=tmp_dir, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(serialized)
        tmp_name = handle.name
    target = index_path(root)
    Path(tmp_name).replace(target)
    write_integrity_hash(root)


def load_index(root: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    index_file = index_path(root)
    if not index_file.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing index.yaml.")
    return load_yaml(index_file)


def resolve_pack_dir(root: Path, pack_id: str, version: str) -> Path:
    return root / "packs" / pack_id / version


def parse_semver(version: str) -> tuple:
    parts = version.split(".")
    if all(part.isdigit() for part in parts):
        return tuple(int(part) for part in parts)
    return tuple(parts)


def ensure_monotonic_versions(versions: List[str]) -> None:
    sorted_versions = sorted(versions, key=parse_semver)
    if versions != sorted_versions:
        raise MirrorError("Pack versions are not monotonic in index.yaml.")


def validate_migration_chain(pack_dir: Path) -> None:
    migrations_dir = pack_dir / "migrations"
    if not migrations_dir.exists() or not any(migrations_dir.iterdir()):
        raise MirrorError("Missing migration files.")


def read_signature_bytes(signature_path: Path) -> bytes:
    raw = signature_path.read_bytes()
    try:
        decoded = base64.b64decode(raw, validate=True)
        if decoded:
            return decoded
    except (ValueError, binascii.Error):
        pass
    return raw


def load_public_key(key_path: Path):
    if not importlib.util.find_spec("cryptography"):
        raise MirrorError("cryptography is required to load public keys.")
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization

    return serialization.load_pem_public_key(key_path.read_bytes())


def verify_signature(key_path: Path, data: bytes, signature: bytes) -> None:
    if not importlib.util.find_spec("cryptography"):
        verify_signature_with_openssl(key_path, data, signature)
        return

    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding, ec
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.utils import decode_dss_signature

    public_key = load_public_key(key_path)
    if hasattr(public_key, "verify"):
        if public_key.__class__.__name__.startswith("_RSAPublicKey"):
            public_key.verify(signature, data, padding.PKCS1v15(), hashes.SHA256())
            return
        if public_key.__class__.__name__.startswith("_EllipticCurvePublicKey"):
            try:
                public_key.verify(signature, data, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))
            except ValueError:
                r, s = decode_dss_signature(signature)
                public_key.verify((r, s), data, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))
            return
    raise MirrorError("Unsupported public key type.")


def verify_signature_with_openssl(key_path: Path, data: bytes, signature: bytes) -> None:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        data_path = Path(tmp_dir) / "data.bin"
        sig_path = Path(tmp_dir) / "sig.bin"
        data_path.write_bytes(data)
        sig_path.write_bytes(signature)
        openssl_path = shutil.which("openssl")
        if not openssl_path:
            raise MirrorError("OpenSSL not available for signature verification.")
        command = [
            openssl_path,
            "dgst",
            "-sha256",
            "-verify",
            str(key_path),
            "-signature",
            str(sig_path),
            str(data_path),
        ]
        completed = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        if completed.returncode != 0:
            raise MirrorError("Signature verification failed via OpenSSL.")


def resolve_key_path(root: Path, pack_meta: Dict[str, Any], signature_dir: Path) -> Path:
    signature_info = pack_meta.get("signature", {})
    key_id = signature_info.get("key_id")
    if not key_id:
        key_id_path = signature_dir / "key_id.txt"
        if key_id_path.exists():
            key_id = key_id_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    if not key_id:
        trusted_keys = sorted((root / "keys" / "trusted").glob("*.pem"))
        if len(trusted_keys) == 1:
            return trusted_keys[0]
        raise MirrorError("Unable to resolve signing key for pack.")
    key_path = root / "keys" / "trusted" / key_id
    if not key_path.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Signing key not found in trusted keys.")
    revoked_path = root / "keys" / "revoked" / key_id
    if revoked_path.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Signing key has been revoked.")
    return key_path


def validate_pack_hashes(pack_dir: Path, pack_meta: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    hashes = pack_meta.get("hashes")
    if not isinstance(hashes, dict) or not hashes:
        raise MirrorError("pack.yaml missing hashes mapping.")
    for rel_path, expected_hash in hashes.items():
        file_path = pack_dir / rel_path
        if not file_path.exists():
            raise MirrorError(f"Missing file referenced in pack.yaml: {rel_path}")
        actual_hash = compute_sha256(file_path)
        if actual_hash != expected_hash:
            raise MirrorError(f"Hash mismatch for {rel_path}.")


def compute_pack_digest(pack_meta: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    hashes = pack_meta.get("hashes")
    if not isinstance(hashes, dict):
        raise MirrorError("pack.yaml missing hashes mapping for digest.")
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for path_key in sorted(hashes.keys()):
        digest.update(path_key.encode("utf-8"))
        digest.update(hashes[path_key].encode("utf-8"))
    return digest.hexdigest()


def load_pack_meta(pack_dir: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    pack_yaml = pack_dir / "pack.yaml"
    if not pack_yaml.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing pack.yaml.")
    return load_yaml(pack_yaml)


def verify_pack(root: Path, pack_id: str, version: str) -> str:
    pack_dir = resolve_pack_dir(root, pack_id, version)
    if not pack_dir.exists():
        raise MirrorError(f"Missing pack directory for {pack_id}@{version}.")
    pack_meta = load_pack_meta(pack_dir)
    if pack_meta.get("pack") != pack_id or str(pack_meta.get("version")) != version:
        raise MirrorError("pack.yaml metadata does not match directory name.")

    validate_pack_hashes(pack_dir, pack_meta)

    signature_dir = pack_dir / "signature"
    signature_file = signature_dir / "pack.sig"
    if not signature_file.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing signature file.")
    key_path = resolve_key_path(root, pack_meta, signature_dir)
    signature_bytes = read_signature_bytes(signature_file)
    pack_yaml = (pack_dir / "pack.yaml").read_bytes()
    verify_signature(key_path, pack_yaml, signature_bytes)

    validate_migration_chain(pack_dir)

    return compute_pack_digest(pack_meta)


def verify_index_and_packs(root: Path) -> None:
    verify_integrity_hash(root)
    index = load_index(root)
    packs = index.get("packs", {})
    if not isinstance(packs, dict):
        raise MirrorError("index.yaml packs section missing or invalid.")
    for pack_id, pack_info in packs.items():
        versions = pack_info.get("versions")
        if not isinstance(versions, list) or not versions:
            raise MirrorError(f"Pack {pack_id} has no versions.")
        versions = [str(v) for v in versions]
        ensure_monotonic_versions(versions)
        for idx, version in enumerate(versions):
            verify_pack(root, pack_id, str(version))
            if idx > 0:
                validate_migration_chain(resolve_pack_dir(root, pack_id, version))


def append_log(path: Path, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps(payload) + "\n")


def build_audit_payload(event: str, session_id: str, command_id: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    payload = {
        "event": event,
        "session_id": session_id,
        "command_id": command_id,
        "timestamp": utc_now(),
    }
    payload.update(kwargs)
    return payload


def init_registry(root: Path) -> None:
    ensure_layout(root)
    if index_path(root).exists():
        raise MirrorError("Mirror already initialized.")
    index_data = build_index()
    write_index_atomic(root, index_data)


def registry_status(root: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not index_path(root).exists():
        return {"status": "uninitialized"}
    try:
        verify_index_and_packs(root)
        status = "verified"
    except MirrorError as exc:
        status = f"invalid: {exc}"
    index = load_index(root)
    pack_count = len(index.get("packs", {}))
    return {"status": status, "packs": pack_count}


def sync_registry(root: Path, source: str | None, url: str | None, actor: str, surface: str) -> None:
    if not source and not url:
        raise MirrorError("Sync requires --source or --url.")

    session_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    command_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    added_packs: list[str] = []
    rejected_packs: list[str] = []

    ensure_layout(root)
    if not index_path(root).exists():
        write_index_atomic(root, build_index())

    local_index = load_index(root)
    local_packs = local_index.get("packs", {})
    if source:
        upstream_root = Path(source).expanduser()
        upstream_index = load_yaml(upstream_root / INDEX_FILENAME)
    else:
        upstream_index = fetch_remote_index(url)

    updates = False
    for pack_id, pack_info in upstream_index.get("packs", {}).items():
        versions = [str(v) for v in pack_info.get("versions", [])]
        if not versions:
            continue
        local_versions = [str(v) for v in local_packs.get(pack_id, {}).get("versions", [])]
        for version in versions:
            if version in local_versions:
                compare_existing_pack(root, pack_id, version, source, url)
        missing = [version for version in versions if version not in local_versions]
        for version in missing:
            try:
                pack_digest = fetch_and_verify_pack(root, pack_id, version, source, url)
                added_packs.append(f"{pack_id}@{version}")
                local_versions.append(version)
                local_versions = sorted(local_versions, key=parse_semver)
                local_packs.setdefault(pack_id, {})["versions"] = local_versions
                local_packs[pack_id]["latest"] = local_versions[-1]
                updates = True
            except MirrorError as exc:
                rejected_packs.append(f"{pack_id}@{version}: {exc}")

        if local_versions:
            ensure_monotonic_versions(local_versions)

    if updates:
        local_index["packs"] = local_packs
        local_index["registry"]["last_verified"] = utc_now()
        write_index_atomic(root, local_index)

    append_log(
        root / AUDIT_LOG,
        build_audit_payload(
            "registry_sync_completed",
            session_id,
            command_id,
            actor=actor,
            surface=surface,
            result="success" if not rejected_packs else "partial",
            added_packs=added_packs,
            rejected_packs=rejected_packs,
        ),
    )
    append_log(
        root / SYNC_LOG,
        build_audit_payload(
            "registry_sync_details",
            session_id,
            command_id,
            added_packs=added_packs,
            rejected_packs=rejected_packs,
        ),
    )
    (root / LAST_SYNC).write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "last_sync": utc_now(),
                "added_packs": added_packs,
                "rejected_packs": rejected_packs,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    if rejected_packs:
        raise MirrorError("Some packs failed verification during sync.")


def fetch_remote_index(url: str | None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not url:
        raise MirrorError("Missing upstream URL.")
    import urllib.request

    index_url = url.rstrip("/") + f"/{INDEX_FILENAME}"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(index_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
        raw = response.read().decode("utf-8")
    if yaml:
        loaded = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
        if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
            raise MirrorError("Remote index.yaml invalid.")
        return loaded
    return parse_simple_yaml(raw)


def compare_existing_pack(root: Path, pack_id: str, version: str, source: str | None, url: str | None) -> None:
    local_pack_meta = load_pack_meta(resolve_pack_dir(root, pack_id, version))
    local_digest = compute_pack_digest(local_pack_meta)
    if source:
        upstream_pack_meta = load_pack_meta(resolve_pack_dir(Path(source).expanduser(), pack_id, version))
    else:
        upstream_pack_meta = fetch_remote_pack_meta(url, pack_id, version)
    upstream_digest = compute_pack_digest(upstream_pack_meta)
    if local_digest != upstream_digest:
        raise MirrorError("Conflict: same pack version has different hash.")


def fetch_and_verify_pack(root: Path, pack_id: str, version: str, source: str | None, url: str | None) -> str:
    if resolve_pack_dir(root, pack_id, version).exists():
        raise MirrorError("Pack already exists locally.")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        temp_root = Path(tmp_dir)
        pack_dir = temp_root / "packs" / pack_id / version
        pack_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        if source:
            upstream_root = Path(source).expanduser()
            source_pack_dir = resolve_pack_dir(upstream_root, pack_id, version)
            if not source_pack_dir.exists():
                raise MirrorError("Pack not found in source mirror.")
            shutil.copytree(source_pack_dir, pack_dir, dirs_exist_ok=True)
        else:
            download_pack_from_url(url, pack_id, version, pack_dir)

        digest = verify_pack_in_temp(root, pack_dir)

        target_dir = resolve_pack_dir(root, pack_id, version)
        target_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copytree(pack_dir, target_dir, dirs_exist_ok=False)

    return digest


def verify_pack_in_temp(root: Path, pack_dir: Path) -> str:
    pack_meta = load_yaml(pack_dir / "pack.yaml")
    pack_id = str(pack_meta.get("pack"))
    version = str(pack_meta.get("version"))
    if not pack_id or not version:
        raise MirrorError("pack.yaml missing pack or version.")
    validate_pack_hashes(pack_dir, pack_meta)
    signature_dir = pack_dir / "signature"
    signature_file = signature_dir / "pack.sig"
    if not signature_file.exists():
        raise MirrorError("Missing signature file.")
    key_path = resolve_key_path(root, pack_meta, signature_dir)
    signature_bytes = read_signature_bytes(signature_file)
    pack_yaml = (pack_dir / "pack.yaml").read_bytes()
    verify_signature(key_path, pack_yaml, signature_bytes)
    validate_migration_chain(pack_dir)
    return compute_pack_digest(pack_meta)


def fetch_remote_pack_meta(url: str | None, pack_id: str, version: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not url:
        raise MirrorError("Missing upstream URL.")
    import urllib.request

    pack_yaml_url = url.rstrip("/") + f"/packs/{pack_id}/{version}/pack.yaml"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(pack_yaml_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
        raw = response.read().decode("utf-8")
    if yaml:
        loaded = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
        if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
            raise MirrorError("Remote pack.yaml invalid.")
        return loaded
    return parse_simple_yaml(raw)


def download_pack_from_url(url: str | None, pack_id: str, version: str, dest_dir: Path) -> None:
    if not url:
        raise MirrorError("Missing upstream URL.")
    import urllib.request

    base_url = url.rstrip("/") + f"/packs/{pack_id}/{version}"
    pack_yaml_url = base_url + "/pack.yaml"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(pack_yaml_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
        pack_yaml = response.read().decode("utf-8")
    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (dest_dir / "pack.yaml").write_text(pack_yaml, encoding="utf-8")
    pack_meta = load_yaml(dest_dir / "pack.yaml")

    hashes = pack_meta.get("hashes", {})
    if not isinstance(hashes, dict):
        raise MirrorError("Remote pack.yaml missing hashes.")
    for rel_path in hashes.keys():
        file_url = base_url + f"/{rel_path}"
        file_path = dest_dir / rel_path
        file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(file_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
            file_path.write_bytes(response.read())

    signature_dir = dest_dir / "signature"
    signature_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    signature_url = base_url + "/signature/pack.sig"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(signature_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
        (signature_dir / "pack.sig").write_bytes(response.read())

    key_id_url = base_url + "/signature/key_id.txt"
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(key_id_url) as response:  # noqa: S310
            (signature_dir / "key_id.txt").write_bytes(response.read())
    except Exception:
        pass


def run_templates_cli(args: Iterable[str] | None) -> int:
    parser = build_templates_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(args)

    templates = filter_templates(args.engine, args.task)
    if not templates:
        parser.error("No templates matched the provided filters.")

    if args.list:
        listing = "\n".join(
            f"{template.engine}:{template.name} - {template.summary}" for template in templates
        )
        write_output(listing, args.output)
        return 0

    if args.format == "json":
        payload = [asdict(template) for template in templates]
        write_output(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), args.output)
        return 0

    if args.all_in_one or len(templates) > 1:
        content = "\n\n".join(format_template(template) for template in templates)
        write_output(content, args.output)
        return 0

    content = format_template(templates[0])
    write_output(content, args.output)
    return 0


def build_registry_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Offline-first registry mirror")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mirror-root",
        default=str(MIRROR_ROOT_DEFAULT),
        help="Registry mirror root path (default: ~/.osl/registry).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--actor",
        default=os.getenv("USER", "unknown"),
        help="Actor name for audit logs.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--surface",
        default="cli",
        help="Surface identifier for audit logs (cli, unity, unreal, ci).",
    )

    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("init", help="Initialize a new mirror layout.")
    subparsers.add_parser("status", help="Report mirror verification status.")
    subparsers.add_parser("verify", help="Verify mirror integrity and packs.")

    sync_parser = subparsers.add_parser("sync", help="Sync mirror from upstream source.")
    sync_parser.add_argument("--source", help="Local path to upstream mirror.")
    sync_parser.add_argument("--url", help="Upstream mirror base URL.")

    return parser


def run_registry_cli(args: Iterable[str] | None) -> int:
    parser = build_registry_parser()
    parsed = parser.parse_args(args)
    root = Path(parsed.mirror_root).expanduser()

    try:
        if parsed.command == "init":
            init_registry(root)
            print(f"Mirror initialized at {root}")
            return 0
        if parsed.command == "status":
            status = registry_status(root)
            print(json.dumps(status, indent=2))
            return 0
        if parsed.command == "verify":
            verify_index_and_packs(root)
            index = load_index(root)
            index["registry"]["last_verified"] = utc_now()
            write_index_atomic(root, index)
            print("Mirror verified")
            return 0
        if parsed.command == "sync":
            sync_registry(root, parsed.source, parsed.url, parsed.actor, parsed.surface)
            print("Mirror sync complete")
            return 0
    except MirrorError as exc:
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    return 1


def main(argv: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> int:
    argv_list = list(argv) if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]
    if argv_list and argv_list[0] == "registry":
        return run_registry_cli(argv_list[1:])
    if argv_list and argv_list[0] == "templates":
        return run_templates_cli(argv_list[1:])
    return run_templates_cli(argv_list)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# 3. Check Python 3.12 availability

if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Error "Python 3.12 NOT FOUND.
Install Python 3.12.x (64-bit) from https://www.python.org and re-run this script."
    exit 1
}

# 4. Go to Auto-Claude directory
$repo = "$HOME\Auto-Claude"
if (-not (Test-Path $repo)) {
    Write-Error "Auto-Claude directory not found at $repo"
    exit 1

# 5. Remove broken venv if exists

    Write-Host "Removing old virtual environment..."
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv
}

# 6. Create clean venv with Python 3.12

py -3.12 -m venv venv

# 7. Activate venv

pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt

# 10. Install test dependencies (non-fatal)

}

# 11. Install node deps if needed

    Write-Host "Installing Node dependencies..."

}

# 12. Run Auto-Claude

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

Write-Host "=== AUTO-CLAUDE WINDOWS HARD FIX ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# Allow scripts
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Force

# Allow py launcher to auto-install
$env:PYLAUNCHER_ALLOW_INSTALL = "1"

# Ensure winget exists
if (-not (Get-Command winget -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Error "winget not found. Update Windows App Installer."
    exit 1
}

# Install Python 3.12 silently if missing
$pyList = py -0 2>$null
if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Host "Installing Python 3.12.x (64-bit)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 --source winget --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements
    Write-Host "Python installed. Restarting shell is NOT required." -ForegroundColor Green
}

# Verify Python 3.12
$pyList = py -0
if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Error "Python 3.12 installation failed."
    exit 1
}

Write-Host "Python 3.12 detected ✔" -ForegroundColor Green

# Move to repo
$repo = "$HOME\Auto-Claude"
if (-not (Test-Path $repo)) {
    Write-Error "Auto-Claude not found at $repo"
    exit 1
}
Set-Location $repo

# Remove old venv
if (Test-Path "venv") {
    Write-Host "Removing old venv..."
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv
}

# Create new venv with Python 3.12
Write-Host "Creating clean venv (Python 3.12)..."
py -3.12 -m venv venv

# Activate venv
Write-Host "Activating venv..."
& "$repo\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1"

# Upgrade tooling
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# Install backend dependencies
Write-Host "Installing backend dependencies..."
pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt

# Install test deps (optional)
if (Test-Path "tests\requirements-test.txt") {
    pip install -r tests/requirements-test.txt
}

# Install Node deps if needed
if (Test-Path "package.json") {
    Write-Host "Installing Node dependencies..."
    npm install
}

# Run correct backend entrypoint
Write-Host "`n=== STARTING AUTO-CLAUDE ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
python apps/backend/main.py

New version has been released! Price will be going up soon, especially once more features are added!

RevoltUnrealPlugin is designed for developers who want to dramatically accelerate their Unreal Engine workflow using AI tools, automation systems, and modern coding assistants. Instead of manually opening assets, hunting through menus, or adjusting dozens of properties by hand, this plugin allows AI-driven tools to handle the repetitive work for you. It creates a direct path for automation, enabling rapid iteration and large-scale content adjustments without the usual editor overhead.

This makes it a powerful companion for anyone using tools like Cursor, local LLMs, custom offline models, or cloud-based AI systems.

Built for AI-Assisted Development

RevoltUnrealPlugin integrates smoothly with AI-first development environments. When paired with systems like Cursor, you can have an AI:





Explore and understand your project structure



Identify assets, characters, weapons, or specific gameplay elements



Generate content variations



Make large-scale adjustments to gameplay parameters



Apply balancing changes across many assets



Create new assets based on patterns you define



Automate entire workflows that normally take hours

The plugin enables AI to operate on your Unreal project in a structured, reliable, and consistent way.

Works With Local and Offline Models

Unlike cloud tools that charge per-token or require ongoing subscriptions, RevoltUnrealPlugin works perfectly with:





Local LLMs running on your machine



Models served through tools like LM Studio, Ollama, or custom inference servers



GPU-hosted models on your own hardware



Self-hosted cloud models that incur no per-request fees

This means you can build a fully automated Unreal workflow with zero ongoing cost, powered entirely by models you control.

Compatible With Any AI Environment

Whether you use Cursor, a Jupyter notebook, a Python script, or a custom-built tool, RevoltUnrealPlugin supports it. If the AI system can reason about your game’s assets or reference your project structure, it can drive high-level tasks such as:





Tuning gameplay systems



Adjusting damage, recoil, movement, or AI behavior



Generating variations of characters or weapons



Creating content for rapid prototyping



Setting up level layouts or spawn patterns



Performing project-wide audits and fixes

This opens the door for AI to become a genuine assistant in your daily development workflow rather than just a code-completion tool.

With this plugin, tasks that previously required opening dozens of blueprints can be completed automatically. Examples include:





Rebalancing every weapon in the game based on a design rule



Creating multiple NPC variants for testing



Updating property values across many assets



Generating content for new gameplay modes



Preparing large batches of assets for prototyping



Building your own automated pipelines and utilities

RevoltUnrealPlugin allows AI systems to operate at scale, making broad changes quickly and safely.

Summary

RevoltUnrealPlugin gives you a faster, more modern way to work with Unreal Engine by connecting your project to AI-driven tools, automation workflows, and local LLMs. It allows you to offload repetitive tasks, accelerate production, and build scalable pipelines without relying on paid APIs or manual asset editing.

Revolt Unreal Plugin — What It Is and What It Does
Core Purpose
RevoltUnrealPlugin is an AI-driven automation plugin for Unreal Engine designed to drastically reduce manual editor work. It allows AI tools to interact directly with Unreal projects so developers can automate repetitive, large-scale, or time-consuming tasks instead of performing them manually inside the editor.

The plugin acts as a bridge between Unreal Engine and AI systems, enabling AI to understand, inspect, and modify Unreal projects in a structured way.

Primary Value Proposition
Instead of developers:

Opening assets one by one

Navigating editor menus

Manually tweaking properties

Repeating the same adjustments across many assets

The plugin allows AI-assisted tools to do that work automatically.

This enables:

Faster iteration

Large-scale changes across a project

Reduced editor overhead

Workflow acceleration

Designed for AI-Assisted Development
The plugin is explicitly built to work alongside AI-first development tools such as:

Cursor

Local LLMs

Offline models

Cloud or self-hosted AI systems

With the plugin in place, an AI can:

Explore and understand project structure

Identify assets, characters, weapons, or systems

Generate content variations

Apply balancing or tuning changes

Modify gameplay parameters at scale

Create new assets based on existing patterns

Automate workflows that normally take hours

This allows AI to function as a true development assistant, not just a code autocomplete tool.

It works with:

Local LLMs running on your machine

Self-hosted cloud models

RevoltUnrealPlugin is a workflow acceleration tool for Unreal Engine that connects AI-driven systems directly to your project. It enables automation, large-scale content changes, rapid prototyping, and AI-assisted balancing without relying on paid APIs or manual editor work.

LEE GIER — you want “everything about the game” in one place, right now, in this chat. Because humans love centralized documentation and then never read it again. Cool. Here’s the full Nyghtshade Hollow game breakdown: what it is, what happens, what the player can do, and all the major systems.

Nyghtshade Hollow
A prison life RPG + survival sim + social manipulation sandbox built around role-play, routine, reputation, and power. It’s not “escape prison.” It’s “survive prison, run prison, or get crushed by it.”

In-lore location: 1900 W Sunshine St, Springfield, MO 65807.
(Yes, it’s real. No, that doesn’t make it less fictional. Humans do this constantly.)

Core pillars
Routine is the battlefield
Schedules, counts, work details, chow, chapel, lockdowns, inspections.

Reputation is currency
Everyone watches. Every choice has social consequences.

Power has layers
Inmates, crews, staff, administration, snitches, outside contacts.

You are never “safe”
Safety is built: alliances, leverage, habits, preparation, reading people.

The player fantasy
You’re an inmate (or in certain modes, staff) trying to climb out of “nobody” status into one of these arcs:

The Survivor: keeps head down, builds stability, gets through time.

The Operator: controls trade, favors, protection, information.

The Enforcer: feared, respected, dangerous.

The Scholar: books, skills, education, legal angle.

The Believer: chapel influence, moral authority, community protection.

The Ghost: stealthy, quiet, contraband runner, unseen mover.

The Kingpin: faction leadership, territory control, runs the Hollow.

The Redeemed: self-change path (hard mode, but meaningful).

Main gameplay loop (minute-to-minute)
Wake → hygiene → count → chow → work/yard → conflict/opportunity → programs → evening chow → showers → night routines → lockdown → late-night schemes

You’re constantly juggling:

Needs (hunger, sleep, hygiene, morale)

Risk (contraband, heat, suspicion)

Status (rep, alliances, debts)

Progress (skills, money, influence)

What the player can do (the big list)
Movement & exploration
Navigate cell blocks, yards, chow hall, gym, chapel, library, medical, admin corridors, visitation, work sites.

Discover restricted routes, staff-only zones, hidden stashes.

Learn schedules and exploit timing windows (counts, shift changes).

Social systems
Talk, persuade, intimidate, deceive, negotiate.

Make allies, rivals, protectors, dependents.

Build “network power”: who owes you, who trusts you, who fears you.

Snitch dynamics: decide what you are, and live with it.

Factions & crews
Join a crew, rise in rank, or stay independent.

Crew benefits: protection, access, work slots, contraband supply, muscle.

Crew costs: obligations, politics, retaliation, forced choices.

Territory control (yard corners, dayroom tables, trade lanes).

Jobs & programs
Work details: kitchen, laundry, janitorial, maintenance, chapel crew, library assistant, medical runner, commissary, yard crew.

Programs: GED, therapy groups, substance recovery, anger management, chapel services.

Each job/program gives access (places, people, tools, info) and progress (skills, reputation, perks).

Contraband & economy
Prison currency: commissary items, favors, phone time, protection.

Contraband types: tobacco/vapes, “paper,” homemade alcohol, meds, phones, shanks, tools, food.

Smuggling routes: work detail access, laundering through trades, hidden stashes, mule networks.

Market manipulation: price gouging, scarcity creation, debt traps.

Crafting
Kitchen crafting (food combos, morale boosts).

Improvised tools (lock picks-ish analogs, stash containers, razor mods).

Weapon crafting (shank variants with different concealment, lethality, break chance).

Tattoo craft (ink mixtures, needles, infection risk system).

Combat (not arcade, not superhero)
Fistfights: grapples, stamina, balance, crowd influence.

Weapons: high risk, high consequence.

“Heat” system: staff response scale depends on your history, witnesses, severity.

Aftermath: medical, segregation, loss of property, faction retaliation.

Stealth & surveillance
Avoid cameras, avoid staff lines of sight, time your movement with noise events.

Plant/steal contraband.

Frame jobs: plant items, fake witnesses, manipulate suspicion.

Legal + time systems
Sentence time, good time, disciplinary time.

Misconducts: write-ups change your access, movement, job eligibility.

“Casework” path: law library, filing, appeals (slow, grindy, powerful if you commit).

Phone, mail, visitation (outside world pressure)
Calls: build outside support or burn bridges.

Mail: info, money orders, emotional boosts, story triggers.

Visitation: relationship management, contraband vectors, narrative choices.

Needs & survival systems (the “living” layer)
Hunger / nutrition
Chow quality varies.

Commissary supplements.

Hunger affects stamina, mood, impulse control.

Trading food becomes an actual economy lever.

Sleep / exhaustion
Noise, threats, stress reduce sleep quality.

Exhaustion affects reaction time, social patience, combat stamina, learning rate.

Hygiene / health
Shower access is schedule- and politics-dependent.

Dirty status affects NPC reactions and disease risk.

Medical: injuries, infections (tattoos, fights), withdrawal.

Mental state
Stress, paranoia, depression, anger, hope.

Your mental state changes dialogue options, aim steadiness, decision speed, and “crack” probability under interrogation.

Progression systems (skills, perks, identity)
Skill trees (examples)
Social: persuasion, intimidation, reading tells, lying, conflict de-escalation.

Combat: boxing basics, grappling, weapon handling, situational awareness.

Stealth: timing, concealment, stash mastery, silent movement.

Tradecraft: pricing, negotiation, debt enforcement, supply chains.

Crafting: kitchen craft, tool craft, weapon craft, tattoo craft.

Education: faster learning, legal research, program boosts.

Faith/Community: morale aura, conflict calming, chapel influence, protection network.

Each skill line feeds real gameplay access, not “+2 damage” nonsense.

Tattoos (not cosmetic fluff)
Tattoos function as:

Reputation signals (who you belong to, what you’ve done)

Perk triggers (fear bonus, loyalty bonus, intimidation boost)

Risk flags (infection chance, staff suspicion, faction attention)

Books & reading
Books give:

Skill XP multipliers

New crafting recipes

Legal knowledge

Mental stability boosts

Dialogue unlocks (you sound smarter, people treat you differently)

Reading takes time, which is a resource, which is the whole point.

World & key characters (known canon pieces)
Bridget Galletti
Official: Bridget Galletti. In-lore: wife of Lee (your in-world tie), Warden with an unusual dual presence that also ties into medical/arts inside the Hollow (she’s an “institution,” not just a title). She’s a power node: rules, mercy, leverage, consequences.

Damian Radcliff
New major character (NPC): a strategic wildcard. The kind of person who can be your ladder or your downfall depending on how you play him.

Harrington Marlowe
85-year-old lifer. War-return tragedy, incarcerated after a violent chain of events involving betrayal and death. He’s a living artifact of prison history: wisdom, bitterness, and old-world prison codes.

Events that “happen” (dynamic story engine)
Instead of one straight plot, Nyghtshade Hollow runs on systems + event arcs:

Daily events
Count shake-ups

Shakedowns

Cell inspections

Random lockdowns

Commissary delays

Yard fights

Medical emergencies

Kitchen shortages

Staff rotation changes

Seasonal/major arcs
Faction war buildup → flashpoints → aftermath

New warden policy shifts → instability → new meta

Contraband drought → economy chaos → new kingmakers

Chapel revival arc (hope vs exploitation)

Informant arc (paranoia spikes, trust collapses)

Riot arc (rare, catastrophic, permanent consequences)

Player-driven arcs
You start a trade ring.

You broker peace or ignite war.

You protect a vulnerable inmate or exploit them.

You rise into leadership or get cut down publicly.

Consequences (because otherwise it’s just cosplay)
Staff memory: they treat you based on your record.

Inmate memory: reputation sticks, even if you “changed.”

Injuries persist.

Debt persists.

Betrayal persists.

If you go violent, the game becomes harder socially and administratively.

Win states (multiple endings)
Not “beat the final boss.” More like outcomes:

Parole/Release: clean-ish path, hard social game, long patience.

Institutional Power: you “win” inside, but you’re stuck inside.

Collapse: segregation spiral, addiction spiral, isolation spiral.

Redemption: you become someone better and survive the place.

Legend: feared/respected name that echoes even when you are moved or gone.

The “feel” of the game
Oppressive but alive.

Moments of humor and humanity in the middle of brutal routine.

Realistic power dynamics: staff have authority, inmates have numbers, everyone has pressure.

import json

# Define file paths for key files
base_path = "/mnt/data/Togpt_extracted"
key_files = [
    "package.json",
    "vite.config.ts",
    "tailwind.config.js",
    "wrangler.json",
    "src/react-app/App.tsx",
    "src/worker/index.ts",
]

file_contents = {}

# Read contents safely
for file in key_files:
    file_path = os.path.join(base_path, file)
    if os.path.exists(file_path):
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            content = f.read()
            # Try to parse JSON files for structure clarity
            if file.endswith(".json"):
                try:
                    file_contents[file] = json.loads(content)
                except:
                    file_contents[file] = content
            else:
                file_contents[file] = content[:2000]  # limit to avoid overload

file_contents.keys()

LEE GIER — you want “everything about the game” in one place, right now, in this chat. Because humans love centralized documentation and then never read it again. Cool. Here’s the full Nyghtshade Hollow game breakdown: what it is, what happens, what the player can do, and all the major systems.

Nyghtshade Hollow
A prison life RPG + survival sim + social manipulation sandbox built around role-play, routine, reputation, and power. It’s not “escape prison.” It’s “survive prison, run prison, or get crushed by it.”

In-lore location: 1900 W Sunshine St, Springfield, MO 65807.
(Yes, it’s real. No, that doesn’t make it less fictional. Humans do this constantly.)

Core pillars
Routine is the battlefield
Schedules, counts, work details, chow, chapel, lockdowns, inspections.

Reputation is currency
Everyone watches. Every choice has social consequences.

Power has layers
Inmates, crews, staff, administration, snitches, outside contacts.

You are never “safe”
Safety is built: alliances, leverage, habits, preparation, reading people.

The player fantasy
You’re an inmate (or in certain modes, staff) trying to climb out of “nobody” status into one of these arcs:

The Survivor: keeps head down, builds stability, gets through time.

The Operator: controls trade, favors, protection, information.

The Enforcer: feared, respected, dangerous.

The Scholar: books, skills, education, legal angle.

The Believer: chapel influence, moral authority, community protection.

The Ghost: stealthy, quiet, contraband runner, unseen mover.

The Kingpin: faction leadership, territory control, runs the Hollow.

The Redeemed: self-change path (hard mode, but meaningful).

Main gameplay loop (minute-to-minute)
Wake → hygiene → count → chow → work/yard → conflict/opportunity → programs → evening chow → showers → night routines → lockdown → late-night schemes

You’re constantly juggling:

Needs (hunger, sleep, hygiene, morale)

Risk (contraband, heat, suspicion)

Status (rep, alliances, debts)

Progress (skills, money, influence)

What the player can do (the big list)
Movement & exploration
Navigate cell blocks, yards, chow hall, gym, chapel, library, medical, admin corridors, visitation, work sites.

Discover restricted routes, staff-only zones, hidden stashes.

Learn schedules and exploit timing windows (counts, shift changes).

Social systems
Talk, persuade, intimidate, deceive, negotiate.

Make allies, rivals, protectors, dependents.

Build “network power”: who owes you, who trusts you, who fears you.

Snitch dynamics: decide what you are, and live with it.

Factions & crews
Join a crew, rise in rank, or stay independent.

Crew benefits: protection, access, work slots, contraband supply, muscle.

Crew costs: obligations, politics, retaliation, forced choices.

Territory control (yard corners, dayroom tables, trade lanes).

Jobs & programs
Work details: kitchen, laundry, janitorial, maintenance, chapel crew, library assistant, medical runner, commissary, yard crew.

Programs: GED, therapy groups, substance recovery, anger management, chapel services.

Each job/program gives access (places, people, tools, info) and progress (skills, reputation, perks).

Contraband & economy
Prison currency: commissary items, favors, phone time, protection.

Contraband types: tobacco/vapes, “paper,” homemade alcohol, meds, phones, shanks, tools, food.

Smuggling routes: work detail access, laundering through trades, hidden stashes, mule networks.

Market manipulation: price gouging, scarcity creation, debt traps.

Crafting
Kitchen crafting (food combos, morale boosts).

Improvised tools (lock picks-ish analogs, stash containers, razor mods).

Weapon crafting (shank variants with different concealment, lethality, break chance).

Tattoo craft (ink mixtures, needles, infection risk system).

Combat (not arcade, not superhero)
Fistfights: grapples, stamina, balance, crowd influence.

Weapons: high risk, high consequence.

“Heat” system: staff response scale depends on your history, witnesses, severity.

Aftermath: medical, segregation, loss of property, faction retaliation.

Stealth & surveillance
Avoid cameras, avoid staff lines of sight, time your movement with noise events.

Plant/steal contraband.

Frame jobs: plant items, fake witnesses, manipulate suspicion.

Legal + time systems
Sentence time, good time, disciplinary time.

Misconducts: write-ups change your access, movement, job eligibility.

“Casework” path: law library, filing, appeals (slow, grindy, powerful if you commit).

Phone, mail, visitation (outside world pressure)
Calls: build outside support or burn bridges.

Mail: info, money orders, emotional boosts, story triggers.

Visitation: relationship management, contraband vectors, narrative choices.

Needs & survival systems (the “living” layer)
Hunger / nutrition
Chow quality varies.

Commissary supplements.

Hunger affects stamina, mood, impulse control.

Trading food becomes an actual economy lever.

Sleep / exhaustion
Noise, threats, stress reduce sleep quality.

Exhaustion affects reaction time, social patience, combat stamina, learning rate.

Hygiene / health
Shower access is schedule- and politics-dependent.

Dirty status affects NPC reactions and disease risk.

Medical: injuries, infections (tattoos, fights), withdrawal.

Mental state
Stress, paranoia, depression, anger, hope.

Your mental state changes dialogue options, aim steadiness, decision speed, and “crack” probability under interrogation.

Progression systems (skills, perks, identity)
Skill trees (examples)
Social: persuasion, intimidation, reading tells, lying, conflict de-escalation.

Combat: boxing basics, grappling, weapon handling, situational awareness.

Stealth: timing, concealment, stash mastery, silent movement.

Tradecraft: pricing, negotiation, debt enforcement, supply chains.

Crafting: kitchen craft, tool craft, weapon craft, tattoo craft.

Education: faster learning, legal research, program boosts.

Faith/Community: morale aura, conflict calming, chapel influence, protection network.

Each skill line feeds real gameplay access, not “+2 damage” nonsense.

Tattoos (not cosmetic fluff)
Tattoos function as:

Reputation signals (who you belong to, what you’ve done)

Perk triggers (fear bonus, loyalty bonus, intimidation boost)

Risk flags (infection chance, staff suspicion, faction attention)

Books & reading
Books give:

Skill XP multipliers

New crafting recipes

Legal knowledge

Mental stability boosts

Dialogue unlocks (you sound smarter, people treat you differently)

Reading takes time, which is a resource, which is the whole point.

World & key characters (known canon pieces)
Bridget Galletti
Official: Bridget Galletti. In-lore: wife of Lee (your in-world tie), Warden with an unusual dual presence that also ties into medical/arts inside the Hollow (she’s an “institution,” not just a title). She’s a power node: rules, mercy, leverage, consequences.

Damian Radcliff
New major character (NPC): a strategic wildcard. The kind of person who can be your ladder or your downfall depending on how you play him.

Harrington Marlowe
85-year-old lifer. War-return tragedy, incarcerated after a violent chain of events involving betrayal and death. He’s a living artifact of prison history: wisdom, bitterness, and old-world prison codes.

Events that “happen” (dynamic story engine)
Instead of one straight plot, Nyghtshade Hollow runs on systems + event arcs:

Daily events
Count shake-ups

Shakedowns

Cell inspections

Random lockdowns

Commissary delays

Yard fights

Medical emergencies

Kitchen shortages

Staff rotation changes

Seasonal/major arcs
Faction war buildup → flashpoints → aftermath

New warden policy shifts → instability → new meta

Contraband drought → economy chaos → new kingmakers

Chapel revival arc (hope vs exploitation)

Informant arc (paranoia spikes, trust collapses)

Riot arc (rare, catastrophic, permanent consequences)

Player-driven arcs
You start a trade ring.

You broker peace or ignite war.

You protect a vulnerable inmate or exploit them.

You rise into leadership or get cut down publicly.

Consequences (because otherwise it’s just cosplay)
Staff memory: they treat you based on your record.

Inmate memory: reputation sticks, even if you “changed.”

Injuries persist.

Debt persists.

Betrayal persists.

If you go violent, the game becomes harder socially and administratively.

Win states (multiple endings)
Not “beat the final boss.” More like outcomes:

Parole/Release: clean-ish path, hard social game, long patience.

Institutional Power: you “win” inside, but you’re stuck inside.

Collapse: segregation spiral, addiction spiral, isolation spiral.

Redemption: you become someone better and survive the place.

Legend: feared/respected name that echoes even when you are moved or gone.

The “feel” of the game
Oppressive but alive.

Moments of humor and humanity in the middle of brutal routine.

Realistic power dynamics: staff have authority, inmates have numbers, everyone has pressure.

Frontend React Example (Dashboard Page):

import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { getGenerations, getCredits } from '../services/api';

const Dashboard = () => {
  const [credits, setCredits] = useState(0);
  const [history, setHistory] = useState([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    getCredits().then(setCredits);
    getGenerations().then(setHistory);
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="p-6 bg-gray-900 text-white min-h-screen">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold mb-4">THE NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW Dashboard</h1>
      <p>Credits: {credits}</p>
      <div className="mt-6">
        {history.map((item: any) => (
          <div key={item.id} className="mb-4 p-4 bg-gray-800 rounded">
            <p>Type: {item.type}</p>
            <img src={item.previewUrl} alt="preview" className="mt-2"/>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

export default Dashboard;

Express server entrypoint (backend/src/index.ts)

import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import authRoutes from './routes/authRoutes';
import generationRoutes from './routes/generationRoutes';
import { connectDB } from './config/db';

const app = express();
app.use(cors());
app.use(express.json());

connectDB();

app.use('/api/auth', authRoutes);
app.use('/api/generation', generationRoutes);

const PORT = process.env.PORT || 5000;
app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT}`));

Stripe Payment Service (backend/src/services/paymentService.ts)

import Stripe from 'stripe';
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY!, { apiVersion: '2025-11-14' });

export async function createPaymentIntent(amount: number, currency: string = 'usd') {
  const paymentIntent = await stripe.paymentIntents.create({ amount, currency });
  return paymentIntent.client_secret;
}

API Service (frontend/src/services/api.ts)

import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'http://localhost:5000/api';

export const login = async (email: string, password: string) => {
  const { data } = await axios.post(`${API_URL}/auth/login`, { email, password });
  return data;
};

export const fetchGenerations = async () => {
  const { data } = await axios.get(`${API_URL}/generation`);
  return data;
};

import { fetchGenerations } from '../services/api';
import GenerationCard from '../components/GenerationCard';

export default function Dashboard() {
  const [history, setHistory] = useState<any[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchGenerations().then(setHistory);
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-gray-900 text-white p-6">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold mb-6">THE NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW</h1>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
        {history.map(item => (
          <GenerationCard key={item.id} generation={item} />
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW
PHASE I: THE CORE BIBLE
Part 1: What the Hollow Is
1. The Nature of Nyghtshade Hollow
Nyghtshade Hollow is not a prison in the conventional sense.

It is not a place designed for rehabilitation, nor is it merely a holding structure for the condemned. It is a self-sustaining human pressure system, engineered to compress behavior, accelerate consequence, and expose truth. Every routine, corridor, policy, and unspoken rule exists to force people into revealing who they really are when escape is not an option.

The Hollow does not ask who you were before you arrived.
It asks who you become when watched, measured, and restricted.

Officially, Nyghtshade Hollow is classified as a maximum-security correctional and containment complex, operating under a hybrid state-federal charter. Unofficially, it is known among staff and inmates alike as a place where people are sent when no one wants to deal with them anymore. The violent. The politically inconvenient. The forgotten. The ones who don’t fit cleanly into systems that prefer neat outcomes.

The Hollow exists because compromise failed.

Where other institutions softened, Nyghtshade Hollow hardened. Where reforms stalled, Nyghtshade doubled down. Its philosophy is simple, brutal, and unapologetic:

Control is not granted.
Control is extracted.

2. Why Nyghtshade Hollow Exists
Nyghtshade Hollow was not built out of optimism. It was built out of exhaustion.

The state was tired of revolving doors.
The courts were tired of appeals.
The public was tired of names reappearing on headlines.

Nyghtshade Hollow is the result of a consensus no one wanted to say out loud: that some individuals do not respond to second chances, and that pretending otherwise costs more lives than it saves.

But there is a deeper truth beneath the official narrative.

Nyghtshade Hollow also exists as an experiment.

Not in the scientific sense with clipboards and white coats, but in the institutional sense. A living model of how order emerges when formal authority is stretched thin and informal power fills the gaps. Administrators study it. Lawmakers quietly reference it. Private contractors learn from it.

The Hollow is watched.

Not constantly. Not openly. But carefully enough that patterns matter.

Every riot, every alliance, every quiet year without incident becomes data.

3. The Core Philosophy
Nyghtshade Hollow operates on four foundational principles. These principles are never posted on walls. They are never explained to inmates. They are learned the hard way.

Principle I: Routine Is Law
Schedules are absolute.
Movement is controlled.
Time belongs to the institution.

Routine is not about efficiency. It is about erosion. By removing choice from the mundane, Nyghtshade Hollow strips inmates of the illusion that freedom exists in small decisions. Wake-up times, meal lines, work assignments, chapel attendance, yard access. All fixed. All enforced.

Break routine, and the system notices.

Respect routine, and the system tolerates you.

Principle II: Power Is Local
Official authority exists, but real power is localized.

Correctional officers control hallways.
Sergeants control shifts.
Unit heads control blocks.

Inmates control each other.

Nyghtshade Hollow does not eliminate inmate hierarchies. It allows them, then monitors how they form. Crews, shot-callers, protectors, predators. The prison understands that suppressing all informal power only guarantees explosions later.

So the Hollow manages imbalance rather than pretending equality exists.

Principle III: Visibility Is Currency
Everything is watched. Not always directly. Not always evenly. But enough that perception becomes as important as reality.

Reputation matters.

An inmate believed to be dangerous gains space.
An inmate believed to be weak loses protection.
A staff member believed to be corrupt becomes leverage.

Surveillance is not just cameras. It is gossip, reports, logs, rumors, and memory. The Hollow remembers.

Principle IV: Mercy Is Strategic
Nyghtshade Hollow does not operate on cruelty for cruelty’s sake. That is inefficient.

Mercy exists, but only when it stabilizes the system. Medical care. Limited privileges. Controlled incentives. These are not kindnesses. They are tools.

Mercy is applied where it reduces resistance and withdrawn where it invites defiance.

No one here is owed compassion.
Some are granted it temporarily.

4. The Illusion of Choice
Nyghtshade Hollow is designed to make inmates believe they are choosing their path.

You can choose who you associate with.
You can choose whether to work or refuse.
You can choose how you respond to provocation.

But every choice exists within constraints engineered to funnel outcomes.

Those who seek dominance are noticed early.
Those who isolate become vulnerable.
Those who cooperate survive longer but lose leverage.

The Hollow does not tell you what to do.

It shows you what happens when you don’t learn.

5. The Psychological Environment
Nyghtshade Hollow is oppressive without being chaotic. That distinction matters.

Noise is controlled.
Lighting is intentional.
Movement is predictable.

There are no constant alarms screaming in the background. No endless riots. No cinematic mayhem. The Hollow’s cruelty lies in its consistency. Days blur. Weeks repeat. Years stack.

The greatest punishment is not violence.

It is monotony under observation.

Inmates begin to measure time by events rather than dates. Count days. Lockdowns. Transfers. Deaths. New arrivals.

Hope does not disappear entirely. It becomes conditional.

6. The Social Contract Inside the Hollow
Unwritten rules govern survival:

Don’t draw attention unless you can survive it.

Pay debts, or disappear.

Respect lines that aren’t marked.

Never assume staff ignorance is kindness.

Snitching is not forbidden. It is priced.

Violence is not constant. It is selective.

Religion exists, not as salvation, but as structure.

The Hollow tolerates belief systems as long as they reduce chaos. When belief becomes influence, it is monitored. When influence becomes power, it is checked.

7. What Nyghtshade Hollow Is Not
Nyghtshade Hollow is not:

A redemption fantasy

A hero’s journey

A sandbox without consequence

A satire of incarceration

It does not care about narrative arcs.

It cares about equilibrium.

Those who adapt become fixtures.
Those who resist become examples.

8. The Player’s Place in the System (Foundational)
The player is not special because they are the player.

They are special only if they earn it.

Nyghtshade Hollow does not bend to protagonists. It reacts to actors. The system treats the player the same way it treats every other body entering intake.

Observation. Classification. Pressure.

From the moment the player arrives, the Hollow begins deciding what kind of problem they are likely to become.

END OF PHASE I – PART 1
Next, Part 2 will cover:

The institutional history of Nyghtshade Hollow

How it evolved over decades

The compromises that shaped its current form

The scars still embedded in its policies and layout

This is canon now. We build forward from here.
